correctness.rationale: Condition on two fixed Pareto weights. Each remaining independent vertex gives one of four two-edge marks; explicitly integrate its four probabilities with the lower Pareto cutoff. The two nonzero single marks and the double mark have intensities mu_w-gamma, mu_v-gamma and gamma in the n epsilon^alpha limit. The rare-cell multinomial-to-independent-Poisson theorem reconstructs the full joint law. Direct tagged edge vanishes; distance exactly two is equivalent in the limit to one or more double marks. The beta-algebra overlap integral and the positive-intensity bounds were reconstructed. Conditional Poisson Chernoff sandwiches with independent Pareto mixing means yield exact sequential joint tail coefficient. The full domain 0<alpha<1, fixed w,v>=1, lambda>0 is covered. check.py ran 225 assertions; finite checks supplement rather than replace proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 capped-Pareto preprint establishes one-vertex degree and macroscopic graph geometry, and its indexed dust argument recognizes common-neighbor correlations; inspected statements do not provide the full tagged degree/codegree law, exact shared-neighbor intensity, or exact distance-two limit. The 2022 earlier paper obtains a related pair-dependence result for a different soft exponential edge kernel and says full joint degree distribution was not explored. The 2016 Lin-Reinert result concerns degree-class counts in independent-edge inhomogeneous graphs. A published prior theorem concerns a capped-Pareto local-clustering atom; its statement does not imply the present conditional Poisson triad. The original 2026 full paper was inaccessible; risk remains documented.

value.rationale: The 2026 graph paper bounds typical large-component distance by three but does not quantify the probability of a two-step connection. The exact shared-hub Poisson parameter gives that probability at fixed weights and the unconditional double-Pareto integral; it also makes a weight-independent common-neighbor fraction for equal weights. Codegree is a natural structural observable governing clustering, distance two and shared exposure. Distinct positive local dependence coexists with a sharp tail-decoupling constant. The result is neither a known-table recomputation nor a parameter-only rebranding of a soft-kernel theorem.
